policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'but unto God' renders the same phrase either way; an added article before theo has no English exponent.
ASV opens 'Now I would have you all speak with tongues' — a de connective; gar would be rendered 'for'.
ASV 'except he interpret' is the English subjunctive required after 'except' and renders subjunctive or indicative alike.
Nyn and nyni are the same adverb; ASV 'But now' does not distinguish them.
ASV 'if they give not a distinction' renders aorist or present subjunctive of the same verb identically.
Word-order variant only; English 'if the trumpet give an uncertain voice' fixes its own order.
ASV 'There are ... so many kinds' follows the neuter plural subject; Greek regularly takes a singular verb with such a subject, so number of the verb is not distinguished.
ASV 'and no kind is without signification' renders no partitive pronoun; the added auton would appear as 'of them'.
Dio and dioper are both rendered 'Wherefore'; the ASV does not distinguish the intensified form.
ASV 'if thou bless with the spirit' renders present or aorist subjunctive alike.
ASV 'with the spirit' fits bare dative, en with dative, or the articular dative; English requires the article and the preposition regardless.
ASV reads 'I thank God', with no possessive; the added mou would be rendered 'my God'.
ASV 'I speak with tongues' is plural, rendering glossais and not the singular glosse.
ASV makes 'I speak with tongues more than you all' an independent finite clause, rendering the indicative lalo rather than the participle lalon.
ASV 'with my understanding' renders the bare dative and dia with the genitive alike.
ASV 'by the lips of strangers' renders the genitive heteron; the dative heterois would give 'with other lips' modifying the lips themselves.
Word-order variant only; ASV 'all speak with tongues' follows English order either way.
ASV has a single 'and so', before 'he will fall down', which renders the kai houtos both texts share; the clause about the secrets of the heart begins without one.
Word-order variant only; ASV 'that God is among you indeed' places 'indeed' by English idiom and does not track the Greek order.
ASV 'each one hath a psalm' renders no genitive pronoun; the added humon would give 'each one of you'.
ASV lists 'hath a revelation, hath a tongue', excluding the RP order that puts tongue first; the two remaining readings differ only in spacing and the English cannot distinguish them.
Both compounds mean 'interpreter'; ASV 'if there be no interpreter' does not distinguish them.
ASV 'let the women keep silence' renders no possessive; the added humon would give 'your women'.
ASV 'it is not permitted' renders present or perfect passive of the same verb alike.
ASV 'but let them be in subjection' is a third-person imperative, rendering hypotassesthosan; the infinitive would continue the preceding clause as 'but to be in subjection'.
ASV 'if they would learn anything' renders aorist or present infinitive of the same verb alike.
Word-order variant only; ASV 'for a woman to speak in the church' follows English order either way.
ASV supplies the noun in the singular, 'they are the commandment of the Lord', rendering estin entole; the plural entolai would give 'commandments' and the bare estin no noun at all.
ASV text 'let him be ignorant' is the imperative agnoeito; its textual note assigns the passive agnoeitai ('he is not known') to many ancient authorities, i.e. not to the text rendered.
ASV 'Wherefore, my brethren' renders the possessive mou, which the omission would leave untranslated.
Word-order variant only; ASV 'forbid not to speak with tongues' follows English order either way.
ASV begins 'But let all things be done', rendering the connective de that the RP reading omits.
